full_text:
**Verdict: KNOWN.** The behaviour is reported for this exact kind of system: a glider on the spectre tiling. The source is a single recent preprint, which I could read directly.

**1. Model family.** This is a cellular automaton (CA) with a four-state outer-totalistic (semi-totalistic) rule on a graph CA. The cells are the tiles of an aperiodic tiling, and neighbours share a vertex. The tiling is the 2023 "spectre", the chiral monotile that needs no mirror tiles. Your companion tiling with mirrored tiles is the "hat". The standard name for the behaviour is a **glider**, meaning a bounded pattern that travels indefinitely. In the source it is also called a "gliding attractor" or "traveller".

**2. Specific behaviour.**
- **Earliest clear source for this tiling.** Edmond (2026), "Gliders on Aperiodic Monotilings: Cellular Automata on the Hat and Spectre", arXiv:2609.22579 (nlin.CG, submitted 18 Sep 2026). Evolutionary search finds gliders on both monotilings. A sliding window regenerates the patch along the flight, and they travel one million rings at constant speed and heading. That matches your 1,000,000 rings and the regenerating window.
- **Headings.** All headings are quantized, to millidegrees, onto a six-spoke compass, the fast axes of the tiling's graph metric. That matches your six headings 60° apart and the tiny heading error.
- **Rule.** The paper's spectre glider is a four-state rule that never enters state 2. A paper excerpt describes it as a pure three-state relay: a head excites wings, a wing beside a head is promoted to the next head, and crowded wings die. That is your rule set: rule 1 creates wings, rule 3 promotes a wing to a head, and rule 2 kills crowded wings. States 0, 1 and 3 match too.
- **Speed.** The paper says all four monotile gliders share the clock of two generations per ring, which is your 0.5 rings per generation.
- **Launch from two-cell seeds.** The paper measures the reach of the gliding attractor from arbitrary two-cell states. That fits your two-tile seeding and launch share.
- **Your "4 distinct rule programs".** The paper says four of the six runs produced cross-radius-verified gliders: three on the hat and one on the spectre. That matches your one spectre rule plus three hat rules.
- **Replication.** The code and records are public (github.com/jamesedmond/monotile-ca). The repository's verification example replays a record on a radius-384 patch, which matches your 384 rings.

I did not compare the two rule tables line by line. The spectre rule in the paper's Table 7 may have differing numeric thresholds. The structure, state set and observables match, so I treat them as equivalent.

**Precedent and context.**
- **Earliest glider on any aperiodic tiling.** Goucher (2012), "Gliders in Cellular Automata on Penrose Tilings", J. Cellular Automata 7, 385–392. It presents the first glider capable of navigating an aperiodic tiling. It inhabits a four-state outer-totalistic CA and works on generic tilings of quadrilaterals. The two-cell head-and-tail seed in that glider is similar to your seed.
- **Closest thing to a review.** I found no dedicated review. Scholarpedia's "Cellular automata" article covers this, noting that Goucher (2012) described a four-state automaton supporting gliders on aperiodic tilings.
- **Related work.** Bailey and Lindsey, "A Game of Life on Penrose tilings" (arXiv:1708.09301), embed Life itself in multigrid tilings. Owens and Stepney studied Life rules on Penrose tilings.

**3. Citations checked against search results.** The title, author and year match for Edmond 2026 (arXiv abstract page), Goucher 2012 (Semantic Scholar and the author's PDF), and Bailey and Lindsey (arXiv).

**5. Confidence: medium-high.**
- **Why high.** The match on rule structure, speed, headings, one million rings and the 4-rule count is essentially one-to-one with a readable source.
- **Caveats.**
  - The source is a single-author arXiv preprint about 6 weeks old, not peer reviewed.
  - Your simulation may be a replication of that paper's record rather than an independent finding.
  - The preprint claims it is the first CA work on these tilings. That claim concerns novelty and is not something I could check.
  - The hat variants use a different tiling, but the paper itself covers them.
